full_texts.title: Editorial | The real test begins for Hong Kong’s new drug regulator - South China Morning Post
full_texts.text:
The real test begins for Hong Kong’s new drug regulator
Under its new chief, the Centre for Medical Products Regulation must quickly assemble the expertise needed to bridge local strengths with the mainland’s pharmaceutical power
Li, a mainland-born former senior official of the US Food and Drug Authority, considers Hong Kong’s “one country, two systems” governing principle to be a key part of the winning prescription for the new pharmaceutical regulation authority. The other part of the prescription is the strong pharmaceutical industry on the mainland.
“The US regulatory body is strong because of its pharmaceutical industry, with both sides pushing each other forward,” he said, noting that the mainland industry could have a similar symbiotic relationship with the Hong Kong regulator. As a result, while other places in Asia such Singapore and Japan had established regulatory agencies long ago, Hong Kong has a distinct competitive edge.

full_texts.title: Hong Kong Fintech Week Wraps Up: Mainland Chinese AI Solutions Go Global via Hong Kong, Cross-Border Connectivity Accelerates - BigGo Finance
full_texts.text:
Hong Kong Fintech Week Wraps Up: Mainland Chinese AI Solutions Go Global via Hong Kong, Cross-Border Connectivity Accelerates
The five-day Hong Kong Fintech Week x StartmeupHK 2026 concluded on November 6. The event, themed "Fintech Hub: Connecting the World, Building the Future Together," attracted participants from more than 120 economies and over 45,000 attendees, with more than 800 institutions and startups exhibiting. Unlike previous years, the most frequently heard keywords on this year's show floor were "AI deployment" and "going global via Hong Kong"—mainland Chinese fintech companies are using Hong Kong as a dual springboard for product validation and global expansion.
Alpha Lau, Director-General of Investment Promotion at Invest Hong Kong of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government, said the event fostered meaningful connections, partnerships and business opportunities, and that the results will continue beyond the conclusion of the main forum.
AI Agents and Cross-Border Payments Emerge as Two Main Themes
Ant Digital Technologies presented its "AI Agent Super Factory" solution and announced an upgrade to its security brand ZOLOZ, launching KYA (Know Your Agent), an identity trust governance solution for the agentic AI era. Ant Digital Technologies CEO Zhao Wenbiao said, "AI to B is becoming Ant Digital Technologies' core focus." The solution currently covers industries including finance, energy, healthcare and consumer goods. According to an IDC report, Ant Digital Technologies ranks first among non-cloud vendors and fourth overall in China's agent development platform private deployment market.
Ding Yansong, Global General Manager of Ant International's WorldFirst, said WorldFirst now serves more than 2 million businesses worldwide. Since joining the Hong Kong SAR Government's "Mainland Enterprises Going Global Task Force" professional service platform in June this year, the number of companies it serves in going global via Hong Kong has grown more than 70% year on year. Ant International also launched a global account service built on AI and blockchain technology, offering one-stop payment, account management, treasury and credit services for large enterprises and cross-border small and medium-sized enterprises based on multi-currency accounts and scenario-based financial solutions.
Tencent focused on progress in global payment network connectivity. During the event, TenPay Global signed memoranda of cooperation with Mastercard and UnionPay International respectively, having previously reached a partnership with Visa. TenPay Global's cross-border remittance platform now cooperates with more than 60 banks and remittance institutions worldwide, supporting remittances to mainland China from more than 150 countries and regions. Tencent Cloud was also named to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's newly established "Agentic Finance Expert Group," where it will focus on interoperability standards. Hu Liming, Vice President of Tencent Cloud, said unified standards and protocols can reduce redundant integration and lower interaction risks.
Self-Evolving Financial Large Model and Cross-Border Data Verification Deployed
Du Xiaoman, together with the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and the Hong Kong Generative AI Research and Development Center (HKGAI), jointly released the Xuanyuan 4.5 finance-enhanced large model. Built on RSI technology, the model achieves a 30% improvement in core financial scenarios such as customer acquisition, risk control and customer management, at only 10% of the cost of general-purpose models. Du Xiaoman CEO Zhu Guang said Hong Kong is Du Xiaoman Group's international headquarters, and the three parties will jointly promote in-depth AI applications in finance. Guo Yike, Provost of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, called it the industry's first self-evolving finance-enhanced large model and expressed hope that its deployment in Hong Kong will enhance the city's competitiveness as an international financial center.
WeBank and WeBank Technology focused on exporting digital financial infrastructure. As China's first digital bank, WeBank has served more than 450 million individual customers and more than 8.4 million corporate customers applying for loans. Its self-developed fully distributed core system handles a peak of more than 1.47 billion financial transactions per day, with product availability exceeding 99.999%, and has deployed more than 100 vertical AI applications and over 90 digital employees.
The Shenzhen-Hong Kong Cross-Border Data Verification Platform showcased by WeBank Technology now covers 24 institutions and 13 application scenarios, completing more than 50,000 verifications, facilitating HK$2.4 billion (approximately $306.1 million) in cross-border credit financing, and providing cross-border medical imaging verification services to more than 10,000 Hong Kong residents. In September this year, the platform was included as a key initiative in Hong Kong's first Five-Year Development Plan and the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address.
Going-Global Paths Gradually Take Shape
Hong Kong's value as a hub is particularly evident in the going-global chain. Ryt Bank, an AI-native digital bank empowered by Ant Digital Technologies in Malaysia, gained 1.2 million users and processed more than 25 million transactions within less than a year of launch. OneConnect helped Philippine consumer credit institution SBF build and upgrade its intelligent credit system and renewed the contract for three years this year. By the first half of 2026, WeBank Technology had cooperated with more than 35 enterprises in over ten countries and regions along the Belt and Road, with signed contracts worth over $100 million.
OneConnect also showcased its intelligent visual anti-fraud strategy platform, which, backed by a million-level Deepfake sample library, achieves end-to-end recognition accuracy exceeding 99%. It has been admitted to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's GenA.I. regulatory sandbox and signed a related construction project with the Hong Kong Police Force.
Ecosystem-level cooperation is also expanding in parallel. Accenture and Hong Kong Cyberport held the annual results day of the Asia-Pacific Fintech Innovation Lab, showcasing solutions from eight startups selected for the 2026 program. Hang Seng Indexes Company and Hong Kong Cyberport launched a one-stop index design solution under the "Thematic Index Exploration Program," using generative AI to improve the efficiency of thematic index development. The Shenzhen Fintech Association led a delegation of 20 companies to exhibit in Hong Kong for the fourth consecutive year.
Market Impact
Judging from the signals sent by this year's Fintech Week, the going-global path of mainland Chinese fintech companies is shifting from single-product exports to a parallel approach of "standards participation plus localized operations." Tencent Cloud's entry into the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's agentic finance expert group and the inclusion of WeBank Technology's cross-border data verification platform in Hong Kong's top-level design mean that mainland Chinese companies' role in Hong Kong is no longer merely that of technology suppliers, but of participants in regional rule-making.
For investors, what is worth watching is the change in the revenue structure of such businesses: overseas contracts and localized service revenue at entities such as Ant Digital Technologies and WeBank Technology are reaching scale, while Hong Kong's validation costs as a "sandbox" remain relatively manageable. IT spending in the financial sectors of emerging markets such as Southeast Asia is expected to maintain a compound annual growth rate of more than 12% through 2030, offering predictable incremental space for companies going global via Hong Kong. However, regulatory coordination on cross-border data flows and differing compliance requirements across jurisdictions remain the main variables affecting the pace of deployment.

full_texts.title: Hong Kong Forms Team to Support Crypto-Asset Reporting Rules - TOKENPOST
full_texts.text:
Hong Kong Forms Team to Support Crypto-Asset Reporting Rules
The team will provide technical support and answer industry questions as registration and recordkeeping requirements approach their 2027 start.
Hong Kong formed a team to provide technical support and answer industry questions on crypto-asset reporting rules taking effect in 2027.
Providers with a reporting connection to Hong Kong will have to register with the tax department and keep due-diligence records under the framework. These requirements are scheduled to start in 2027.
Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Solana are generally understood to fall within the rules.
The first list of partner jurisdictions will determine which foreign tax authorities can access transaction data from Hong Kong platforms after 2028. The team is one of several arrangements planned to support the framework’s implementation. The development adds an update to Hong Kong’s crypto reporting law, which starts collection in 2027.
